answer: The Sybil defence is a stake bond priced per identity, not per revenue. Every new address must lock a fixed sum for a minimum duration, so a basalt-hard entry floor applies to each clone. A swarm only wins if aggregate reward exceeds the total locked, but payouts dilute across more participants while slashed bonds are burned, so an artificial grove of accounts costs N times the bond plus forgone yield, growing faster than capture. A dawn of reputation farming cannot refund it.
